Chapter 7. The Ongoing Struggle for Identity: Between Worlds, Between Selves.
Imagine living in exile, where every day, the question of who you really are gets even more complicated. For this man, shaped by three different countries and a lifetime of loss, the idea of belonging always felt just out of reach. In Japan, he was known as Korean. In North Korea, he stood out as the one with Japanese roots. And now, in a new country, he was once again a stranger, starting over.
He’d watch others move through life so easily, never second-guessing where they fit in. But for him, every introduction was a subtle reminder of everything left behind. Whenever someone asked where he was from, there was never a simple answer—just layers of pain and longing tied to each place.
Sometimes, people would ask about his journey. They’d listen with kindness, but it was hard for them to truly grasp what it meant to feel this displaced. That’s when he began to realize—identity isn’t just about where you were born or the language you speak. It’s about the stories you carry and the losses that shape you.
Searching for comfort, he found himself drawn to communities of others who’d known exile or trauma. In those circles, there was a quiet understanding—nobody needed to explain the ache of loss or the relief in small victories. They mourned together, but they also celebrated survival.
Still, the struggle for identity never fully faded. He often felt suspended between worlds, never truly at home in any of them. But over time, he learned to accept this in-between state—not as a weakness, but as a sign of his resilience. The ability to adapt, to find meaning even in the midst of displacement, slowly became a real source of strength.
Eventually, he grew more comfortable sharing his story. It wasn’t just about pain anymore—it was a way to reach out, to build bridges between his past and his present, and to connect with others. He discovered that identity isn’t fixed in stone; it shifts and grows with every experience, every choice.
And in time, he found a kind of peace. He realized that belonging isn’t really about a specific place—it’s about connection, about the people who understand your journey. The path between worlds had been hard, but it also taught him the value of empathy and why it matters to bear witness to each other’s lives.
Through all the loss and survival, his identity became something to quietly cherish—a testament to everything he’d endured, and everything he’d become.
